stories.label: Great Pyramid of Giza
stories.text: A tomb built as a mountain of limestone. Nothing to reuse, nothing to repair: sheer mass is its survival plan.

stories.label: Parthenon
stories.text: A temple, then a church, then a mosque, then a powder store that blew up in 1687. It survives as a ruin, not a building.

stories.label: Pantheon
stories.text: A Roman temple that became a church in the 7th century. Continuous use kept its concrete dome roofed.

stories.label: Hagia Sophia
stories.text: Church, mosque, museum and mosque again. It changed faith but never lost its job, or its roof.

stories.label: Colosseum
stories.text: An arena turned quarry, fortress and housing. What was not robbed for stone stands as a ruin.

stories.label: Angkor Wat
stories.text: A Hindu, then Buddhist temple in Cambodia, never fully abandoned.

stories.label: Westminster Abbey
stories.text: Founded before 1100, but the abbey church you see is largely Gothic, rebuilt from the 13th century.

stories.label: Tower of London
stories.text: A Norman keep that stayed useful: royal palace, prison, armoury, treasury, museum.

stories.label: Lighthouse of Alexandria
stories.text: One of the most famous lost buildings: brought down by earthquakes. Wikidata records it as destroyed.

stories.label: Kiyomizu-dera
stories.text: Founded in 778; the timber halls standing today were rebuilt in the 1630s, as Japanese temples often are.

stories.label: Hadrian's Wall
stories.text: A frontier wall of stone and turf. Long stretches were robbed for farm buildings and a road.

stories.label: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
stories.text: Founded in the 4th century, burned, wrecked and rebuilt, but always a place of worship.
